clue.text: Embargo on information that could relieve child's anxiety

definitions.meaning: a blanket ban on news, imposed for safety reasons, keeps details from leaking out
a comfort blanket or cuddly toy that a small child clings to for reassurance

explanation.surface: A news ban that might stop a youngster worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a total news blackout for safety reasons and the comforting cloth a toddler carries everywhere.

clue.text: Leader of troop enters old Persian capital in support

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the leading letter goes into the capital's name

parts.note: Susa was an ancient capital of the Persian Empire

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The head of a band of soldiers comes into an ancient city, offering help.
explanation.walkthrough: Susa, in modern Iran, was a royal capital of the Achaemenid Persian kings.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going or bear its weight is to support it.

clue.text: Youngster, one trying to catch others in the distance

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior scout
in the game of tag, the player who chases is called it

explanation.surface: A child playing tag tries to catch others far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient measure of length based on the forearm, so it is a unit of distance.

clue.text: Rough up and throw off campus

definitions.meaning: in architecture, to give stonework a deliberately rough surface
to send a student away from university for a while as punishment

explanation.surface: Beat someone and expel them from university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough up' looks like beating someone, but it is the masonry sense; sending down a student is a British university term.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers giving stone a rough finish and suspending an undergraduate from college.

clue.text: Feebler batsmen disheartened Sri Lankan

indicators.note: disheartened means having its heart, the middle letter, removed

parts.note: the Tamils are an ethnic group of Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: Weaker cricketers dismayed a player from Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle M of TAMIL. In cricket the weaker batsmen bat last.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the lower-order, weaker batsmen are called the tail of the batting side.

clue.text: Head of tribe in difficult situation in African republic

indicators.note: the second in means placed inside, so the tight spot goes into the country

parts.note: Benin is a republic in West Africa
a jam is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A tribal chief in trouble in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link word. Benjamin, son of Jacob, gave his name to one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin was a son of Jacob and the founding father of one of the tribes of Israel.

clue.text: A Greek mountain covering a hectare

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means coming above, so the mountain is placed on top

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A mountain in Greece extends over a hectare of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Greek' means the Greek letter A. 'a' before 'hectare' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet corresponds to our A.

clue.text: Understanding a small amount is risky

definitions.meaning: the proverb says a little learning is a dangerous thing

explanation.surface: Grasping only a little is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning and awareness is understanding, and the proverb warns that a little of it is dangerous.

clue.text: Collector of shopping even picked up bread inside

indicators.note: inside says the bread goes into the middle of the other piece
in a down clue, picked up means read upwards, so the word for even is reversed

parts.note: yet can mean even, as in 'yet more'
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A shopper even collected some bread inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had stray OCR words; the page prints the clue shown. 'picked up' turns the word for even into TEY, and 'inside' fills it with the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket cart gathers up the goods being bought, so it is a collector of shopping.

clue.text: Viola's brother seen with nurse touring Corsican port

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the nurse's letters travel around the port's

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse
Bastia is a port on the north-east coast of Corsica

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean character's brother is spotted with a nurse on a trip to Corsica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen with' are link words. In Twelfth Night, Viola's twin brother is shipwrecked and turns up in Illyria.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Twelfth Night the heroine Viola has a twin brother bearing this name.

clue.text: Concert given zero publicity

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A concert attracts no press attention at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link word; the Proms are a famous London summer series of concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotional piece or advert is informally called by this clipped word for publicity.

clue.text: Girl has a short walk

indicators.note: short means the word for walk loses its final letter

parts.note: to stride is to walk with long steps

explanation.surface: A young woman takes a brief stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word; 'short' trims the last letter, E, from STRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scandinavian female name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Correspondence suggesting inability to make projected meeting

definitions.meaning: correspondence in the sense of a similarity or analogy between two things
lines of this kind, however far they are projected, never meet

explanation.surface: A letter explaining that someone cannot make a planned appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suggesting' links the two. 'Correspondence' looks like letters, and 'projected' like planned, but here it means extended, as geometry lines are.
explanation.definitionFit: A similarity between two cases is called this, and lines of this kind never meet however far they run.

clue.text: Make mistake, incurring as-yet-undecided fine

indicators.note: incurring is read as taking something on board, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to nod is to make a slip, as in 'even Homer nods'
TBA stands for to be arranged or announced, not yet decided

explanation.surface: Someone makes an error and gets a fine whose size has not yet been set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty, but it is the definition in the sense of all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is pretty good or quite acceptable is a mild way of calling it fine.

clue.text: What soundly nails profit?

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word for nails is to be heard, not read

parts.note: tacks are small nails
a return is the profit made on an investment

explanation.surface: A question about what securely fastens down gains.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the form you file tells the taxman about your profit, and so nails it down.
explanation.definitionFit: The form declaring income to the authorities pins down a person's profit for taxation.

clue.text: Potter's interest in jolly super railway

parts.note: wizard is old British slang for excellent or jolly super

explanation.surface: Someone's hobby is a really excellent railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. 'Potter' suggests a pottery maker or snooker player, but it is Harry Potter, the boy wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter studies magic at Hogwarts, so magical skill is his main interest.

clue.text: Shaw briefly a captain, for example, but not of this skilful soldier

indicators.note: briefly says the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Artie Shaw was an American jazz clarinettist and bandleader

indicators.note: but not says the following little word is removed

parts.note: a captain is an example of an officer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A summary of Shaw as a captain, yet not of this able military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims ARTIE to ARTI; 'but not' takes OF from OFFICER, leaving FICER. 'this' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled mechanic in the armed forces, so a skilful soldier.

clue.text: Greek hero cut a plant

indicators.note: cut says the hero's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Achilles was the great Greek hero of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior cuts down a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Achillea is the yarrow genus, named after Achilles, who is said to have used it to heal wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Achillea is a genus of flowering plants, including yarrow.

clue.text: Cathedral architect keeps one cross, a piece of old silver

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the architect's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Sir Basil Spence designed the new Coventry Cathedral
I is the Roman numeral for one
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An architect of a cathedral holds onto a single crucifix, plus an antique silver coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sixpence was a pre-decimal British coin worth six old pennies, struck in silver until 1947.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British sixpenny coin was minted in silver before 1947, making it a piece of old silver.

clue.text: Ancient instrument is picked up to play, not seriously

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted upwards, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: to strum is to play casually or idly

explanation.surface: An old instrument is taken up to be played casually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns IS into SI. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sistrum is a rattle used in ancient Egypt, an ancient musical instrument.

clue.text: Wise woman starting to name vowels in order

parts.note: A and E are the first two vowels
then means next in sequence
A and E are the first two vowels

explanation.surface: A clever woman begins listing the vowels one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting to name' links: name the first vowels in order, A THEN E.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene was the Greek goddess of wisdom, the wise woman of Olympus.

clue.text: No such possible chance of being from this planet

definitions.meaning: 'no ... chance' means no chance at all
belonging to the world rather than heaven

explanation.surface: There is no prospect of being from here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of being' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of the world, and it fills the phrase 'no ___ chance'.

clue.text: Nepotist fails to improve rate of advance

indicators.note: fails tells us the word nepotist breaks down and its letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone who favours relatives does not make progress quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; 'fails' scrambles NEPOTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone to hurry or go faster, so it means to speed up progress.

clue.text: Magazine, having nothing left, beginning to fail

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing
to die can mean to start to fail, like a dying battery

explanation.surface: A magazine with no money left is starting to go under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word. The Oldie is a British humour magazine for older readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oldie is a British monthly magazine, so this names a magazine.

clue.text: Involvement with a female, blonde

parts.note: fair hair is blonde

explanation.surface: Being entangled with a fair-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; the surface hints at a romance, which is also a sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter or business someone is concerned in is an involvement in it.

clue.text: Bikini, say, visible to everyone around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for everyone wraps the other

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A skimpy swimsuit on view to all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' is not the swimsuit but the Pacific atoll used for nuclear tests. 'visible' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands is an example of a ring-shaped coral island.

clue.text: Economist in factory

definitions.meaning: John Stuart ... was a famous economist and philosopher
a factory or works, such as a cotton or steel works

explanation.surface: An economics expert at a manufacturing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: J. S. Mill was a famous economist, and the word also means a factory or works.

clue.text: Pitch not good for this stage of competition

indicators.note: not says the letter for good is to be left out

parts.note: a sports pitch is a ground

explanation.surface: A poor playing surface is unsuitable for a stage of a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; take G from GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is divided into rounds, each a stage of competition such as the third round.

clue.text: Colin strangely reluctant to put on garment

indicators.note: strangely says the name Colin appears in an odd rearranged form

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Colin oddly does not want to get dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put on' is a link phrase; COLIN rearranged gives LOINC.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple cloth wrapped about the hips is a basic item of clothing.

clue.text: Random sort of method to pull oneself together for driving test

parts.note: the Monte Carlo method uses random sampling to solve problems
to rally is to recover one's strength or composure

explanation.surface: A haphazard approach to regaining composure before a driving exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. The surface suggests a learner's exam, but the test is a famous motor rally.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous rally is a demanding motoring event, a gruelling test of drivers.
